metrics.label: Points
metrics.desc: Constructors' points as awarded (Grand Prix, sprint and fastest-lap points of every car).

metrics.label: Points per race
metrics.desc: Points divided by rounds entered.

metrics.label: Wins
metrics.desc: Grand Prix wins by either car.

metrics.label: Podiums
metrics.desc: Podium finishes by any car.

metrics.label: Poles
metrics.desc: Pole positions by any car.

metrics.label: One-twos
metrics.desc: Races the team finished first and second.

metrics.label: Both cars in the points
metrics.desc: Share of rounds in which every car that started scored points.

metrics.label: Average best-car finish
metrics.desc: Mean finishing position of the team's better-placed classified car. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Average best-car grid
metrics.desc: Mean starting slot of the team's better-placed car. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Expected points
metrics.desc: Sum of the walk-forward forecast's expected points for the team's cars.

metrics.label: Points v expected
metrics.desc: Points minus expected points, summed over the team's car-races.

metrics.label: Car race pace (% v field)
metrics.desc: The car part of the season's race-pace decomposition, in percent of the lap against the field (negative is faster), averaged over the rounds it was observed. The car's level is a random walk from round to round, so upgrades and circuit swings show up as movement. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Car race-pace rank
metrics.desc: Mean rank of the car's race-pace state among the teams at each round (1 = fastest). Lower is better.

metrics.label: Car qualifying pace (% v field)
metrics.desc: The car part of the qualifying-pace decomposition, percent of the lap against the field. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Car qualifying-pace rank
metrics.desc: Mean rank of the car's qualifying-pace state at each round. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Car pace trend (%)
metrics.desc: Car race pace over the last third of the rounds minus the first third, percent of the lap. Negative means the car got faster relative to the field. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Car race pace, latest (%)
metrics.desc: The car's race-pace state at the latest modelled round, percent of the lap. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Top speed (km/h)
metrics.desc: Mean of the team's drivers' top speed-trap readings, km/h.

metrics.label: Speed-trap rank
metrics.desc: Mean speed-trap rank of the team's drivers. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Minimum corner speed v field (km/h)
metrics.desc: Mean of the team's drivers' minimum-corner-speed deltas against the field (telemetry), km/h.

metrics.label: Straight-line bias
metrics.desc: Straight-line v cornering profile: z-score of top speed minus z-score of minimum corner speed across the teams. Positive means a car quicker on the straights than through the corners (low drag); negative a downforce car. Descriptive rather than good or bad.

metrics.label: Tyre management index
metrics.desc: Mean of the team's drivers' tyre management index (milliseconds per lap per lap of age better than the field median degradation).

metrics.label: Degradation: soft (s/lap/lap)
metrics.desc: Mean soft-compound degradation of the team's drivers, seconds per lap per lap of age. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Degradation: medium (s/lap/lap)
metrics.desc: Mean medium-compound degradation, seconds per lap per lap of age. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Degradation: hard (s/lap/lap)
metrics.desc: Mean hard-compound degradation, seconds per lap per lap of age. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Pit stop, stationary (median)
metrics.desc: Median stationary time of the team's pit stops (OpenF1, wheels stopped to wheels moving). Lower is better.

metrics.label: Best pit stop
metrics.desc: Fastest stationary pit stop of the season. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Stops under 2.5 s
metrics.desc: Share of the team's stationary times under 2.5 seconds.

metrics.label: Slow stops (> 4 s)
metrics.desc: Stops with a stationary time over 4 seconds. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Pit-lane time (median)
metrics.desc: Median time from pit entry to pit exit for the team's stops. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Pit-lane time v field
metrics.desc: Median over races of the team's median pit-lane time minus the race's median, milliseconds. Negative means quicker through the pit lane than the field. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Pit stops
metrics.desc: Pit stops made by the team's cars.

metrics.label: Places gained through the stops
metrics.desc: Places gained through the pit stops against the race's norm, per car-race: for each stop, running position the lap before it minus running position two laps after it, less the race's average for a stop.

metrics.label: Stops per car-race
metrics.desc: Stops per car-race.

metrics.label: Finish rate
metrics.desc: Share of the team's starts that ended classified.

metrics.label: DNF rate
metrics.desc: Share of the team's starts that ended unclassified. Lower is better.

metrics.label: DNFs
metrics.desc: Retirements and disqualifications. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Mechanical DNFs
metrics.desc: Retirements recorded as mechanical. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Car share of points (Shapley)
metrics.desc: How much of the team's model-expected points the car explains, from a Shapley split of simulated expected points between the car and each driver: |car| / (|car| + sum of |drivers|).

metrics.label: Lead driver's share of points
metrics.desc: Share of the team's points scored by its top-scoring driver. Near 0.5 is a balanced line-up.

metrics.label: Qualifying head-to-head balance
metrics.desc: Share of qualifying head-to-heads won by the team's stronger qualifier. Near 0.5 is a close pairing.
